newsitem.title: UK: Toad shares tumble 32 pct as CEO resigns.
newsitem.headline: Toad shares tumble 32 pct as CEO resigns.

text.p: Shares in auto security products group Toad Plc tumbled 32 percent on Monday as the company said chief executive Charles Parker had quit and warned that sales were below budget in the last two months.
Toad shares were quoted down 19-1/2p at 41-1/2, 64 percent below their year's high of 116p, though no trading was recorded in the stock.

Parker's resignation, due to what the company called "irreconcilable differences", came just five weeks after his appointment as chief executive, and took effect from February 7, Toad said in a statement.
Toad non-executive Director Kevin Gray will take over as caretaker CEO until a suitable replacement is found.
Company sales during December and January "were substantially below budget largely (on)... disappointing retail sales through the Install and dealer networks," the statement added.

Toad's said it expected second-half turnover to March 31 1997 to be below that achieved in the first six months ended September 30 1996, although pre-tax losses before exceptional charges for the second half would be significantly reduced due to improved gross margins.
